units: <cite ref="Berakhot 60a:28">Ber. 60ᵃ</cite> (in a prayer) <he>כי אל ר׳ נאמן וכ׳</he> for thou. O God, art a faithful physician, and thy healing is perfect.

<cite ref="Berakhot 60a:29">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 21:19">Ex. XXI, 19</cite>) <he>מכאן … רשות לר׳ וכ׳</he> from this we learn that a physician is authorized to heal (that healing is not considered an interference with divine dispensation).
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 26b:10">Ab. Zar. 26ᵇ</cite> <he>עיר שאין בה ר׳ ישראל וכ׳</he> a place which has no Jewish surgeon (for circumcision) but has a Samaritan and a gentile surgeon &c.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 27a">Ib. 27ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>ר׳ מומחה</he>, v. <cite ref="M00520"><he>מוּמְחֶה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 4:4">Bekh. IV, 4</cite> (<cite ref="Bekhorot 28b:13">28ᵇ</cite>) <he>תודוס הר׳</he> Thodos (Theodorus) the physician; a. fr.—Pl. <he>רוֹפְאִים</he>, <he>רוֹפְאִין</he>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Ohalot 4:2">Tosef. Ohol. IV, 2</cite> <he>נכנס תיאודורוס הרופא וכל הר׳ עמו</he> Theodorus the physician came in and all the other physicians with him.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 80a:4">B. Kam. 80ᵃ</cite> <he>שאלו לר׳ וכ׳</he> they consulted the physicians who said, there is no remedy for him except &c.; <cite ref="Temurah 15b:46">Tem. 15ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 4:13">Kidd. IV, 13</cite> (<cite ref="Kiddushin 82a:8">82ᵃ</cite>) <he>טוב שבר׳ וכ׳</he> the best of physicians will go to Gehenna (v. Rashi a. l.); a. fr.
